_comment: Capacity DERIVED FROM GROWTH (capacity_level_prior.form=crowding): K = kappa(x) * (R0 - 1)_+, so the Beverton-Holt term becomes F_eff = Fmax/(1 + N/kappa) and N* = kappa*(R0-1). Absence can only come from R0 <= 1 (a sink): run_19/19e turned K into an absence switch (40% of lambda-suitable cells Allee-dead, K fold-range 5e5-6e7) that the coupling prior could not stop. kappa0 = exp(alpha_k), prior median set so K at R0 = 2 is the measured 2.6183-route-count occupied median.

Otherwise run_19 (exchangeable manifold, survival amplitude scale 1.0263, no dispersal noise), with the coupling LOOSENED to logit-normal around 0.6, sd 0.5: tight coupling existed to stop the K switch, which the crowding form now removes structurally (run_19's data put rho at ~0.56).
run_20a: CONSTANT crowding (modifier_bound 0). Most parsimonious: abundance is a pure function of growth. K's manifold column is unused here (prior-only).
